purpose: Static donor catalogue, provenance and observed finite regression mapping for existing Synexia owners.

scope.review_role: second stacked PR: catalogue documentation and metadata only
scope.primary_pr_scope: implementation, donor tests and existing replay

lookup_workflow.action: Inventory existing Synexia source, recipe, compiler, native and fixture owners; bind the baseline and contract before looking for external replacement candidates.

For Java syntax, types, compiler integration and lexical rules, consult the primary JDK API/JLS/OpenJDK source first. For source transformations and recipe cycles, consult OpenRewrite primary docs/source and the already pinned artifact first.
Evaluate other GitHub FOSS donors only for a specific uncovered capability; record exact file/revision, file license, input domain, behavior and why an existing owner cannot already supply it.
Lookup problem/category metadata in LeetCode first. Record exact problem identity, operation, domain, indexing and output/exception contract; do not collect solutions as implementation authority.
Lookup the corresponding category in HackerRank second. Keep its regex dialect, whole-match/search semantics and published constraints as a separate record.
Lookup the corresponding category in GeeksforGeeks third. Treat unavailable statement bodies as unresolved metadata; never fill gaps from a similar problem name.

Compare candidates serially for one file/private atom with its contract sealed. Category similarity only nominates candidates; resolved interfaces, behavior, license and measured evidence decide eligibility.

Make the reusable Maven/OpenRewrite recipe and its regression fixtures the work product. Produce the target candidate deterministically and retain diff, ordered verification logs, hashes, corpus coverage and replay evidence.

category_boundaries.rule: A literal metacharacter is data. Regex metacharacters change the language; quoting policy must be explicit.
Whole-input acceptance and finding a substring are distinct observable operations.
Wildcard star consumes an arbitrary sequence; restricted-regex star repeats its predecessor.
A small dot/star language does not define Java flags, groups, backreferences, boundaries or all Unicode behavior.
Engine substitution requires a proven eligible shared subset and locked API/exception semantics.
Regex/string matches cannot authorize edits inside comments/literals or unrelated owner/overload bindings.
Balanced delimiters do not establish lexical or syntactic validity; Unicode escapes are processed before tokenization.
Java String indices use char code units. JNI strings and byte-oriented native inputs require explicit encoding and coordinate contracts.
Passing every declared finite case proves that corpus observation only; it does not prove every possible Java input.
Hashes bind evidence and detect exact identity; similarity or equal signatures do not establish behavior.

execution.evidence_kind: completed existing Maven/Surefire logs plus inspected test source
counting_rules: Every number in counts_per_mode describes the same declared corpus executed separately in off and required modes.
247 literal pairs and 1477 regex pairs are different families. 1724 is not a literal-pair count.
JUnit discovered tests, logical pairs, representations and operation checks are different units.
Literal API checks are five operations per character representation or UTF-8 slice; native-search API checks are one additional byte-array owner call per slice.
Regex checks are matches and find across three character representations and two UTF-8 layouts: ten checks per pair.
Positive automaton compilation refusal is a failure, never a skipped or passed matching case.
Eleven valid unsupported/budget expressions, six malformed expressions and six literal boundary refusals remain separate from positive pairs.
Native-search API calls include Java pre-dispatch early returns. Actual JNI entries are uninstrumented and are not inferred from the 988 API checks.
The required run asserts native availability. MIndexRegexAutomaton remains Java code in either run.
